# Complete subgap spectroscopy by uniform Sylvester localization

Proposed proof, 2026-11-03. Independent audit requested. This is a restricted massive-bath result, not an efficient general excited-state or extensive-interaction theorem.

## Assumptions and statement

Let H=dΓ(h)+V on fermionic Fock space (optionally tensored with a finite-dimensional impurity of dimension d_I). Assume gI≤h≤RI, g>0, and V is bounded, self-adjoint, globally even, and supported on the impurity and the CAR algebra of an m-dimensional bath source space S. Set v=||V|| and E0=inf spec H. Both particle-number-nonconserving and strong interactions are allowed. All parity sectors must be included in E0 and in the intermediate annihilation map. Fix 0<δ<g and a=g−δ.

Block Krylov spaces K_L=span{S,hS,...,h^(L−1)S} have dimension ≤mL. Let Π_L project onto the full Fock space on K_L with its orthogonal complement in vacuum, retaining the entire finite impurity. The compressed Hamiltonian is H_L=Π_L HΠ_L restricted to ran Π_L. It is an actual Galerkin compression, not an ad hoc chain modification.

Choose α=log(1+δ/(4R)), C=4 sqrt(m) v/δ, η_L=C exp(−αL), and b=2mR. Then for the full spectral projector P=1_[E0,E0+a](H),

  ||(1−Π_L)P|| ≤ η_L.

For η_L<1, P has finite rank ≤d_I 2^(mL). In particular the bottom is an eigenvalue, without a prior ground-existence assumption. If λ_k≤E0+a is the kth full eigenvalue, counting multiplicity, and μ_k is the kth eigenvalue of H_L, then

  λ_k ≤ μ_k ≤ λ_k + ε_L,
  ε_L=(2a η_L²+bη_L)/(1−η_L²).

The lower bound is the minmax principle and supplies the no-spurious-level guarantee. For t≤E0+a and ε_L small,

  N_H(t−ε_L) ≤ N_HL(t) ≤ N_H(t).

A sharp count is certified only when the requested cutoff is separated from a true eigenvalue by the approximation allowance. Ground-aligned excitation energies differ by at most ε_L because both λ_k and λ_1 are shifted upward by numbers in [0,ε_L]. For a finite matrix input h, computing a block Krylov compression and diagonalizing its full Fock matrix yields polynomial cost in bath size and 1/ε at fixed m,d_I,R/δ,v. Explicitly L=O((R/δ) log[(1+sqrt(m)v/δ)(1+mR)/ε]), and matrix dimension is d_I exp(O(mL)). This is not uniform polynomial complexity as m or R/δ grows, and a continuum input still needs a certified one-particle matrix-element oracle.

## Result

The enormous uniform localization depth is unnecessary for *a posteriori* spectral certification when a small selected bath passes a computable complement-energy gate. For the U=4, Delta=1, D=2, Gamma=0.5 superconducting Anderson benchmark, a retained bath of 12 spin modes (total Fock dimension 16384) passes the gate up to excitation 0.8: complement lower-bound candidate lies 0.998997 above the retained ground. Lower/upper Schur matrices both have three low levels below the 0.8 threshold (ground doublet plus singlet). The isolated singlet absolute-energy interval has width 0.002079 from this inexpensive version. These conclusions use numerically observed eigenvalues and need certified matrix arithmetic before being called certificates. The 16-spin-mode test completed in 110.94 seconds (full Fock dimension 262144): ground interval candidate [-2.183242395495,-2.183242383671], singlet interval candidate [-1.647861709560,-1.647657250438], and excitation interval candidate [0.535380674111,0.535585145057], width 0.000204471. Thus the numerical Schur gate reaches the requested 0.001 energy tolerance with 16 bath spin modes. Complement clearance is q-mu0=0.998999960641 and the 0.8-window count sandwich again agrees on three levels. Full-Fock construction was resource-heavy; symmetry-restricted implementation is the next necessary improvement. These are not rigorous numerical certificates until quadrature, ground lower bounds and eigenvalue-index validation are paid.

# Exact-arithmetic audit and unresolved adaptive gate

A genuinely rigorous finite-bath baseline now exists in `exact_inertia_audit.py` and its JSON output. It certifies the specified U=4, N=2 midpoint physical electron Hamiltonian, not the 600-node Gauss bath or continuum. The full dimension is 64; all seven spin sectors (20,15,15,6,6,1,1) are included. No Lanczos or floating-point diagonalization enters the proof.

The only irrational matrix coefficient is t=sqrt(1/pi). Machin's identity and rational alternating-series remainders enclose pi; integer square-root inequalities enclose t in an interval of width 10^-16. The rational surrogate differs from the exact physical Hamiltonian in operator norm by at most 4*10^-16, because there are four hopping operators, each of norm one. Exact Fraction LDL elimination computes inertia, with rational cutoff shifts when a zero pivot occurs. Rational bisection plus Weyl's inequality gives ordered eigenvalue enclosures and certifies completeness. Printed decimal intervals are illustrative; the exact rational intervals in JSON are the proof data.

Result: a ground doublet, next excitation in approximately [0.627287240589,0.627287573675], fourth ordered level above 1.2065846. The count below the true ground plus 0.8 is exactly three, using counts at both enclosing ground-shifted cutoffs. Measured elapsed time is in JSON (about 2–3 seconds here). This is slower than the prior ordinary floating-point small-matrix runs and is a different bath size. It establishes neither a competitive runtime nor convergence to the continuum.

## How to certify the adaptive q and count, without circularity

For every retained-sector effective Hamiltonian, choose a proposed rational lower bound b and prove H_eff-b I positive definite by interval LDL with all pivots positive, or exact rational LDL after enclosing the physical matrix by a surrogate and a norm radius r. In the latter case prove H_eff,surrogate-(b+r) I positive definite. Do this in every sector, not only the candidate ground sector. Then q=b+s is a certified tail threshold. An accurate approximate ground vector may propose b but cannot validate it. Gershgorin lower bounds are valid alternatives, but need not pass the gate.
